title: Best Odds Screen (2026)
verdict: An odds screen is the professional's view of the market: every book's number on one grid, moving in real time. The best odds screen in 2026 is TerminalUp's board, because it is the only screen where the numbers are executable: best fee-adjusted price and size per outcome across nineteen live venues, and an order ticket that routes to the best of them.

Among read-only screens, Unabated is the sharpest, Don Best is the classic, SpotOdds is the fastest on alerts and OddsJam is the broadest. All four are excellent at showing you the move. None can get you down on it.

ranking.fit: Bettors who want a screen they can trade from, covering sportsbooks, exchanges and prediction markets together.
ranking.lacks: A $10,000 minimum. No line-history charts of the kind a classic screen shows.
ranking.note: Per outcome: best fee-adjusted price, available size, bounded ladder with venue counts, raw top of book, and an honest status when a market is thin or stale. Cross-venue fills. 0.5% commission per trade, no subscription.

why: A screen's job is to show you the market honestly. TerminalUp's board does that with rules most screens skip: prices are fee-adjusted before they are compared, so a venue's headline number is never shown as better than what you would actually get; size at each level is shown, so a great price for $200 is not confused with a great price for $20,000; and a market whose evidence has aged out is marked stale with an empty ladder instead of showing an old number as current.

Then it does what no screen does. The order ticket routes your stake to the best venue and across several when the best is thin. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Nineteen venues are live as of November 2026, sixteen more are in the pipeline.
Commission is 0.5% per trade, 0.35% at the highest volume, no subscription and no screen fee. TerminalUp never takes a position, so the screen has no reason to shade anything.
